sentences.en: Dear boss, I keep on hearing the police have caught me, but they won't fix me just yet.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的老板，我总听人说警察抓住我了，但他们可没法这么快就治服我。

sentences.en: I've laughed when they look so clever and talk about being on the right track.
sentences.zh: 他们自作聪明、谈论着正走在正确的线索上时，我简直笑掉大牙。

sentences.en: That joke about leather apron gave me real fits.
sentences.zh: 那个关于皮围裙的笑话可把我逗得前仰后合。

sentences.en: I'm down on whores and I shan't quit ripping them till I do get buckled.
sentences.zh: 我恨透了那些妓女，在我被抓进局子之前，我绝不会停下开膛破肚的活儿。

sentences.en: Grand work, the last job was.
sentences.zh: 干得真漂亮，上一单活儿就是。

sentences.en: I gave the lady no time to squeal.
sentences.zh: 我没给那女士一点尖叫的时间。

sentences.en: How can they catch me now?
sentences.zh: 现在他们怎么可能抓得到我？

sentences.en: I love my work and I want to start again.
sentences.zh: 我热爱我的工作，我想重新开始了。

sentences.en: You will soon hear of me with my funny little games.
sentences.zh: 你们很快就会听到我和我那些有趣的小把戏了。

sentences.en: I saved some of the proper red stuff in a ginger beer bottle over the last job to write with.
sentences.zh: 上回干活时，我在一个姜汁啤酒瓶里留了点真正的红色液体用来写信。

sentences.en: But it went thick like glue and I can't use it.
sentences.zh: 但它变得像胶水一样浓稠，我没法用了。

sentences.en: Red ink is fit enough, I hope.
sentences.zh: 红墨水应该也凑合吧，希望如此。

sentences.en: Ha ha!
sentences.zh: 哈哈！

sentences.en: The next job I do, I shall clip the lady's ears off and send to the police officers just for jolly.
sentences.zh: 我下回干活时，要把那女士的耳朵割下来寄给警官们，纯粹为了好玩。

sentences.en: Wouldn't you?
sentences.zh: 你们难道不会吗？

sentences.en: Keep this letter back till I do a bit more work.
sentences.zh: 把这封信压下别发，等我再多干点活。

sentences.en: Then give it out straight.
sentences.zh: 然后再直接公布出去。

sentences.en: My knife's so nice and sharp.
sentences.zh: 我的刀又漂亮又锋利。

sentences.en: I want to get to work right away if I get a chance.
sentences.zh: 只要有机会，我马上就想开工。

sentences.en: Good luck.
sentences.zh: 祝好运。

sentences.en: Yours truly, Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 你诚挚的，开膛手杰克。

sentences.en: Don't mind me giving the trade name.
sentences.zh: 别介意我用了这个行当的名号。

sentences.en: P.S.
sentences.zh: 附言。

sentences.en: Wasn't good enough to post this before I got all the red ink off my hands.
sentences.zh: 刚才手上还没把红墨水洗干净，所以没法把这封信寄出去。

sentences.en: Curse it.
sentences.zh: 真该死。

sentences.en: No luck yet.
sentences.zh: 目前还没走运。

sentences.en: They say I'm a doctor now.
sentences.zh: 他们说我现在是个医生了。

sentences.en: Ha ha.
sentences.zh: 哈哈。

sentences.en: So that's the most notorious, the most infamous letter in the history of crime.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是犯罪史上最臭名昭著、最声名狼藉的一封信。

sentences.en: And of course it's so chilling because of the mocking, sadistic tone.
sentences.zh: 当然，它之所以让人不寒而栗，是因为那种嘲弄、施虐的语气。

sentences.en: The tone almost of banter.
sentences.zh: 那种几乎带有调侃意味的语气。

sentences.en: And it was sent on the 27th of September, 1888 to the Central News Agency of London.
sentences.zh: 它于 1888 年 9 月 27 日被寄给伦敦中央新闻社。

sentences.en: And they sat on it for two days, unsure whether it was authentic, and then forwarded it to Scotland Yard.
sentences.zh: 他们压了两天没发，不确定它是真是假，随后把它转交给了苏格兰场。

sentences.en: And this is the letter, Tom, that gives the name to somebody who at that point had killed probably two, possibly three,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，正是这封信，给那个当时在伦敦东区臭名昭著、充斥着贫困、犯罪和卖淫的白教堂街区，已经杀害了可能两名、也许三名，

sentences.en: possibly more women on the streets of Whitechapel in an area of the east end of London that was notorious for poverty and crime and prostitution.
sentences.zh: 甚至更多女性的凶手冠上了这个名字。

sentences.en: And both of these women had had had their throats cut and both had been hideously mutilated.
sentences.zh: 这两名女性都被割断了喉咙，并且都被极其残忍地肢解了。

sentences.en: And then after the letter reached Scotland Yard, in the early hours of the 30th of September, the killer struck again, not once, but twice the so-called double event.
sentences.zh: 在这封信到达苏格兰场之后，在 9 月 30 日的凌晨，凶手再次作案，不是一次，而是两次，也就是所谓的“双重事件”。

sentences.en: You know, one of the most dramatic nights in the history of London.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是伦敦历史上最戏剧性的夜晚之一。

sentences.en: And then we come to the most horrific murder of all, which was on the 9th of November, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 然后我们迎来了最恐怖的一起谋杀案，也就是发生在 11 月 9 日的那起，对吧？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that was, again, a woman eviscerated, but this time not on the streets as the other victims of the Whitechapel murderer had been,
sentences.zh: 那又是一位被开膛破肚的女性，但这一次不是像白教堂杀手的其他受害者那样死于街头，

sentences.en: but in a cramped and mean room in a place called Miller's Court in the dark heart of Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 而是在白教堂黑暗核心一个叫做米勒斯法院（Miller's Court）的地方一间逼仄简陋的房间里。

sentences.en: And to those who saw that victim, it seemed, even compared to the previous victims, a vision of hell.
sentences.zh: 对于那些看到那个受害者的人来说，即使跟之前的受害者相比，这也宛如人间地狱。

sentences.en: So one of the witnesses was a woman who had lived above the victim, so directly above the murder scene.
sentences.zh: 其中一位目击者是一位住在受害者楼上的女性，也就是直接住在案发现场的正上方。

sentences.en: And she said, I could bear to look at it only for a second, but I can never forget the sight of it if I live to be 100.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我只敢看上一秒钟，但如果我能活到 100 岁，我都无法忘记当时的景象。”

sentences.en: And another, the man who had forced the locked door of the victim's room, he said, the sight we saw, I cannot drive away from my mind.
sentences.zh: 另一位是撬开受害者房门的人，他说：“我们看到的景象，我怎么也挥之不去。”

sentences.en: It looked more like the work of a devil than of a man.
sentences.zh: “与其说是人类所为，倒更像是恶魔的暴行。”

sentences.en: But as it turns out, almost certainly, although maybe not, but almost certainly, the horror of that murder, the horror of Miller's Court,
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，几乎可以肯定——尽管也并非绝对，但几乎可以肯定，那场谋杀的恐怖，米勒斯法院的恐怖，

sentences.en: seems to have been the climax of Jack the Ripper's reign of terror.
sentences.zh: 似乎成了开膛手杰克恐怖统治的最高潮。

sentences.en: And the thing that people found eerie about that reign of terror wasn't just the brutality, but the ability of the murderer always to be one step ahead of the police,
sentences.zh: 人们对那场恐怖统治感到诡异的地方，不仅在于其残酷性，还在于凶手总能领先警察一步，

sentences.en: to avoid apprehension, to avoid almost being seen.
sentences.zh: 能够逃避搜捕，甚至几乎不被任何人看到。

sentences.en: And now, with this terrible murder in Miller's court, he kind of vanishes as though into thin air,
sentences.zh: 而现在，随着米勒斯法院这起可怕的谋杀案，他某种程度上消失得无影无踪，

sentences.en: and he leaves behind him what I think is undoubtedly the most enduring mystery in the annals of crime.
sentences.zh: 留下了我认为毫无疑问是犯罪史上最经久不衰的谜团。

sentences.en: Would you agree?
sentences.zh: 你同不同意？

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对同意。

sentences.en: He's the one serial killer whose name is known across the world, who appears in films and video games, as we shall talk about, and novels and all sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 他是唯一一个名字世界闻名的连环杀手，正如我们接下来要谈到的，他出现在电影、电子游戏、小说以及各种各样的媒介中。

sentences.en: And I guess, even at the time, there was something otherworldly about him, wasn't there, to people in London.
sentences.zh: 我想，即使在当时，对伦敦人来说，他身上也有一种超乎寻常的特质，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, people would describe him right from an early stage.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们从很早期就开始描述他。

sentences.en: This isn't sort of back projection.
sentences.zh: 这并不是后人的事后追溯。

sentences.en: People would talk about him as a ghost slipping through the streets of the East End, as a ghoul or a vampire kind of feeding on the blood.
sentences.zh: 人们会把他描述为像幽灵一样在东区街头穿梭的鬼魂，或者是靠吸血维生的食尸鬼或吸血鬼。

sentences.en: Yeah, they literally use the word vampire.
sentences.zh: 对，他们字面意思上就用了“吸血鬼”这个词。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: So, there's a quote, isn't there, from the East London Advertiser.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一个引文，来自《东伦敦广告报》（East London Advertiser），对吧？

sentences.en: What can be more appalling than the thought that there's a being in human shape, stealthily moving about a great city, burning with a thirst for human blood,
sentences.zh: “有什么比这种想法更骇人听闻：一个拥有人形的怪物，在伟大的城市中潜行，燃烧着对人血的渴望，

sentences.en: and endowed with such diabolical astuteness as to enable him to gratify his fiendish lust with absolute impunity.
sentences.zh: 并且具备如此恶魔般的狡猾，以至于能够肆无忌惮地满足他那恶魔般的贪婪而完全免受惩罚。”

sentences.en: And it's the sort of combination of the horror, but also the stealth, that he is, I mean, especially the night when he kills two people,
sentences.zh: 这就是恐怖与潜行的结合，他——尤其是他连杀两人的那一晚，

sentences.en: that he is moving from one scene to another like a wraith in the night, you know, completely undetected.
sentences.zh: 他像暗夜中的幽灵一样从一个案发现场移动到另一个案发现场，你知道的，完全没有被察觉。

sentences.en: He must know the area like the back of his hand.
sentences.zh: 他一定对那个地区了如指掌。

sentences.en: He's always one step ahead of the police.
sentences.zh: 他总是领先警察一步。

sentences.en: And for people at the time, that was both horrifying, but also kind of darkly fascinating, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 对于当时的人们来说，这既令人毛骨悚然，又有一种黑暗的迷人之处，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, in that, the thirst for human blood, I mean, there's something vampiric,
sentences.zh: 我是说，那种对人血的渴望，里面带有某种吸血鬼的色彩，

sentences.en: but there's also a kind of a hint of almost cannibalism because organs are being excised and there are rumours that they're being eaten by the killer.
sentences.zh: 但同时也隐约带有一点食人族的意味，因为他的器官被切除了，而且有传言说凶手把它们吃掉了。

sentences.en: So, it does seem something very primordial.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实显得非常原始。

sentences.en: But at the same time, there is a feeling that this is something perhaps expressive of modernity.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，人们也有一种感觉，这或许也是现代性的一种体现。

sentences.en: So, there's another newspaper that says of Jack the Ripper, perhaps he is some mysterious and awful product of modern civilisation.
sentences.zh: 因此，另一家报纸在谈到开膛手杰克时说：也许他是现代文明产下的某种神秘而可怕的产物。

sentences.en: So, people are wondering, what is it about our industrial society that is producing such a monster?
sentences.zh: 所以人们在纳闷，我们的工业社会究竟有什么问题，才会孕育出这样的怪物？

sentences.en: And we've said that Jack the Ripper is the most famous serial killer.
sentences.zh: 我们说过，开膛手杰克是最著名的连环杀手。

sentences.en: I think almost the most intriguing thing about him from the historical point of view is he's actually the first serial killer we know about.
sentences.zh: 我认为从历史的角度来看，他最耐人寻味的一点在于，他其实是我们所知的第一个连环杀手。

sentences.en: I mean, presumably, there were serial killers before him, but he is the first person who is identified as a serial killer in the sense that we understand it today in 2025.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在他之前大概也有连环杀手，但他是在 2025 年我们今天所理解的意义上，第一个被识别为连环杀手的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, there were people previously who'd killed an awful lot of people, so in the Middle Ages or whatever, but there was not the sense of a serial killer phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 对，以前也有过杀害大量人口的人，比如在欧洲中世纪等等，但当时并没有“连环杀手”这种现象的概念。

sentences.en: And he invents the phenomenon, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 是他发明了这种现象，对吧？

sentences.en: Or rather, the newspaper editors who write about him invent the phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，是那些报道他的报纸编辑们发明了这种现象。

sentences.en: Or the psychiatrists who kind of home in on what he represents as a particular kind of monster.
sentences.zh: 或者是精神病学家们，他们聚焦于他作为一种特定怪物的代表性。

sentences.en: And they classify what he might be in scientific terMs.
sentences.zh: 他们用科学术语对他的本质进行分类。

sentences.en: And I think that's also a part of the story.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是故事的一部分。

sentences.en: So, for all these reasons, he's notorious.
sentences.zh: 出于所有这些原因，他臭名昭著。

sentences.en: But I think there are two obvious reasons why he remains such a notorious figure still almost 150 years on.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，时隔近 150 年，他依然是一个如此声名狼藉的人物，有两个显而易见的原因。

sentences.en: The first, the most obvious, is that he was never caught.
sentences.zh: 第一点，也是最明显的一点，是他从未被抓获。

sentences.en: So, his identity remains a mystery to this day.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的真实身份至今仍是个谜。

sentences.en: And we will be exploring the range of possible suspects in our final episode of this five-part series.
sentences.zh: 我们将在本五集系列的最后一集探讨各种可能的嫌疑人。

sentences.en: Surely, solving the mystery and unveiling the killer.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，我们将解开谜团并揭开凶手的面纱。

sentences.en: Yes, we will.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们会去的。

sentences.en: But also, I think that name, Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 但同时，我认为那个名字——开膛手杰克。

sentences.en: I mean, it's so horribly, brilliantly memorable.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这个名字既可怕又绝妙，让人过目难忘。

sentences.en: We will be returning to that letter and other letters that were thought by the police at the time,
sentences.zh: 我们将重新审视那封信以及当时警察认为可能是由凶手寄出的其他信件，

sentences.en: perhaps to have been sent by the murderer, asking whether they really were, were they authentic or were they faked.
sentences.zh: 探讨它们是否真的是凶手所写，它们究竟是真是假。

sentences.en: There are lots to come.
sentences.zh: 精彩内容还在后头。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对的。

sentences.en: So, we've got lots of episodes to come.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们后面还有很多集节目。

sentences.en: But just on the sort of history of the study of Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 但就研究开膛手杰克的历史而言。

sentences.en: So, Jack the Ripper was a literary phenomenon right from the beginning as much as he was a kind of a physical one.
sentences.zh: 开膛手杰克从一开始就是一个文学现象，其程度不亚于他作为一个现实存在的实体。

sentences.en: Because most people experience the Ripper story through the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人都是通过报纸来了解开膛手的故事的。

sentences.en: And ever since, you know, people have written, I mean, people have written about him.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，人们一直在书写，我是说，人们一直在书写关于他的故事。

sentences.en: They've never stopped writing about him.
sentences.zh: 他们从未停止过对他的书写。

sentences.en: So, there's an Australian journalist in 1929, isn't there, called Leonard Matters, who wrote one of the first big studies of the murders.
sentences.zh: 所以，1929 年有一位澳大利亚记者，对吧，名叫伦纳德·马特斯（Leonard Matters），他写了关于这些谋杀案最早的大型研究之一。

sentences.en: And he said, if a journalist cannot sell anything else in London, he can always sell a story about Jack the Ripper.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果一个记者在伦敦什么都卖不出去，他总能卖出一篇关于开膛手杰克的故事。

sentences.en: And it's interesting he's Australian because it's a reminder that Jack the Ripper is properly a global story.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是他是澳大利亚人，这提醒我们，开膛手杰克其实是一个全球性的故事。

sentences.en: People are fascinated by this and, you know, huge topic of fascination in the English-speaking world, but even beyond the English-speaking world as well.
sentences.zh: 人们对此着迷，你知道的，这是英语世界的一个巨大迷恋话题，甚至在英语世界之外也是如此。

sentences.en: And to this day, the idea that if you want to sell a book, you come up with a theory about who Jack the Ripper was, I mean, it remains the case.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，如果你想卖出一本书，只要抛出一个关于开膛手杰克是谁的理论，这种情况依然屡试不爽。

sentences.en: And there's this entire field, ripperology.
sentences.zh: 而且还诞生了一个完整的领域——开膛手学（ripperology）。

sentences.en: It's a kind of sub-genre of the true crime genre.
sentences.zh: 这算是真实罪案流派下的一个子流派。

sentences.en: Which, for the brutality exercised on the victim, is even more shocking.
sentences.zh: 这起案件对受害者施加的残忍行径更加令人震惊。

sentences.en: And will no doubt create as great a sensation in the vicinity as its predecessor.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，它将在附近地区引起同前案一样巨大的轰动。

sentences.en: The affair, up to the present, is enveloped in complete mystery.

sentences.en: And the police have as yet no evidence to trace the perpetrators of the horrible deed.

sentences.en: So that was the Central News Agency reporting on the 31st of August, 1888, the news of what it headlined,
sentences.zh: 以上是中央新闻社在1888年8月31日对以下头条新闻的报道，

sentences.en: A Horrible Murder in Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 《白教堂发生可怕谋杀案》。

sentences.en: So Tom, take us through the story of this new murder.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆，请给我们讲讲这起新谋杀案的经过吧。

sentences.en: Okay, so the body had been found by a delivery man, car man, as the Victorians call it.
sentences.zh: 好的，尸体是由一名送货员（维多利亚时代的人称之为马车夫）发现的。

sentences.en: And he worked for Pickford's in Covent Garden.
sentences.zh: 他在科芬园的皮克福德公司工作。

sentences.en: And he'd been heading to work from Bethnal Green through Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 他当时正从贝思纳尔格林经由白教堂去上班。

sentences.en: And he was off to Covent Garden in central London.
sentences.zh: 他要去伦敦市中心的科芬园。

sentences.en: And he found the body around 3.40 a.m.
sentences.zh: 他在凌晨3点40分左右发现了尸体。

sentences.en: This was a guy called Charles Lechmere.
sentences.zh: 这个人名叫查尔斯·莱克米尔。

sentences.en: And he was walking to work down Bucks Row, which is, I mean, it's no longer called Bucks Row, but it's still there.
sentences.zh: 他正沿着巴克斯罗步行去上班，我的意思是，这条路现在已经不叫巴克斯罗了，但它依然还在。

sentences.en: You can still walk down the street.
sentences.zh: 你还是可以顺着这条街走。

sentences.en: Very narrow in Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 在白教堂（Whitechapel）一带非常狭窄。

sentences.en: And as he's doing so, he sees this object lying beside the entrance to a stable yard.
sentences.zh: 正当他这么做时，他看到这个物体躺在马厩院入口旁边。

sentences.en: And it is now one of the entrances to Whitechapel tube station.
sentences.zh: 而现在它是白教堂地铁站的其中一个入口。

sentences.en: But at the time, it was what was called a yard crossing.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这被称为庭院交叉口。

sentences.en: So a kind of narrow alleyway leading off the main street into a stable yard.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种狭窄的小巷，从主街通往马厩院。

sentences.en: And so he stops, he goes to inspect it, and he finds that it is the body of a woman.
sentences.zh: 于是他停下脚步，过去查看，发现那是一个女人的尸体。

sentences.en: And he stands there irresolutely wondering what to do.
sentences.zh: 他犹豫不决地站在那里，盘算着该怎么办。

sentences.en: And as he does so, he's joined by another car man, a guy called Robert Paul, who is also on his way to work.
sentences.zh: 正当他这么做时，另一个车夫加入了他，这人名叫罗伯特·保尔（Robert Paul），他也是在去上班的路上。

sentences.en: And one of the themes, I think, of this entire series will be the number of people who are either coming back or going to work throughout the night.
sentences.zh: 我认为，整个系列的主题之一，将是整夜来来往往或去上班的人数众多。

sentences.en: The streets of Whitechapel are very, very busy.
sentences.zh: 白教堂的街道非常非常繁忙。

sentences.en: So they both approach the body, which is huddled in the shadows.
sentences.zh: 于是他们俩走近那具蜷缩在阴影中的尸体。

sentences.en: It's still, you know, it's still nighttime.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当时仍然是深夜。

sentences.en: And they find that the woman is lying on her back.
sentences.zh: 他们发现那个女人是仰面躺着的。

sentences.en: Her skirts have been hitched up over her hips.
sentences.zh: 她的裙子被掀到了臀部以上。

sentences.en: And Lechmere can't bring himself to touch the body.
sentences.zh: 而莱克米尔（Lechmere）怎么也鼓不起勇气去触碰尸体。

sentences.en: But Robert Paul does.
sentences.zh: 但罗伯特·保尔做了。

sentences.en: And he finds that her skin is cold to the touch.
sentences.zh: 他发现摸上去她的皮肤是冰冷的。

sentences.en: But he presses his ear to her mouth.
sentences.zh: 但他把耳朵贴在她的嘴边。

sentences.en: And he fancies that he can hear her breathing.
sentences.zh: 他觉得好像能听到她在呼吸。

sentences.en: Now, both men are late for work.
sentences.zh: 此时，两名男子上班都迟到了。

sentences.en: So they smooth down the woman's skirts.
sentences.zh: 于是他们抚平了女人的裙子。

sentences.en: And they head on their way.
sentences.zh: 然后继续赶路。

sentences.en: And a short distance on, they run into a policeman.
sentences.zh: 走了不远，他们遇到了一名警察。

sentences.en: And they tell him what they've found.
sentences.zh: 他们把发现的情况告诉了他。

sentences.en: And Lechmere says, she looks to me to be either dead or drunk.
sentences.zh: 莱克米尔说，在我看来她要么是死了要么是醉了。

sentences.en: But for my part, I think she is dead.
sentences.zh: 但就我而言，我认为她已经死了。

sentences.en: And so she is.
sentences.zh: 事实确实如此。

sentences.en: She is very, very dead.
sentences.zh: 她死得彻彻底底、不能再死了。

sentences.en: And they haven't noticed the details.
sentences.zh: 而他们没有注意到细节。

sentences.en: I guess because, what time did you say it was?
sentences.zh: 我想是因为，你刚才说那是几点？

sentences.en: It's 3.40 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 那是凌晨3点40分。

sentences.en: So dawn is not yet broken.
sentences.zh: 所以天还没亮。

sentences.en: So it's dark.
sentences.zh: 因此一片漆黑。

sentences.en: But when the police arrive, and they do notice the details.
sentences.zh: 但当警察到达时，他们确实注意到了这些细节。

sentences.en: And the details, which are rehearsed at the inquest, are, as they will be throughout this series.
sentences.zh: 这些在死因研讯中反复提及的细节，正如它们贯穿整个系列一样。

sentences.en: I mean, no surprise.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，并不意外。

sentences.en: They are really gruesome and really, really shocking, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们真的极其可怕、非常非常令人震惊，对吧？

sentences.en: They are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So listeners should be warned.
sentences.zh: 所以应该对听众发出警告。

sentences.en: So the victim's throat had been cut almost from ear to ear.
sentences.zh: 受害者的喉咙几乎被从左到右割断了。

sentences.en: The abdomen had been savagely ripped open, exposing the intestines.
sentences.zh: 腹部被残忍地剖开，内脏都露了出来。

sentences.en: The lining of the woman's stomach had been cut in several places.
sentences.zh: 女人的胃壁有多处被割破。

sentences.en: There were also, and I quote the details of the inquest, two small stabs on private parts, apparently done with a strong bladed knife.
sentences.zh: 还有——我引用研讯的细节——私密处有两个小刺伤，显然是用一把锋利的刀造成的。

sentences.en: And the surgeon who conducted the autopsy, a doctor called Rhys Llewellyn, he said, he confessed himself to be appalled by what he had been examining.
sentences.zh: 进行尸检的外科医生，一位名叫里斯·卢万（Rhys Llewellyn）的医生说，他坦言自己对所检查过的一切感到震惊。

sentences.en: I have seen many terrible cases, but never such a brutal affair as this.
sentences.zh: 我见过许多可怕的案件，但从未见过如此残忍的事件。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that's important to bring across right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为从一开始就把这一点传达出来很重要。

sentences.en: I mean, we don't want to wallow in the details of these crimes, but it is important to convey how horrific they are, to explain what the public reaction is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们不想沉溺于这些罪行的细节中，但传达它们的恐怖程度、解释公众的反应是很重要的。

sentences.en: You know, these are not murders like any other.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这些不是普通的谋杀案。

sentences.en: I mean, there are stabbings are not uncommon in London in the 1880s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在1880年代的伦敦，持刀行凶并不少见。

sentences.en: You know, there are dozens every year of people stabbed to death.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每年都有几十人被刺死。

sentences.en: But there is something uniquely savage and bestial about Jack the Ripper's murders.
sentences.zh: 但开膛手杰克的谋杀案中有一种独一无二的野蛮和兽性。

sentences.en: Literally visceral.
sentences.zh: 简直是直击内心的。

sentences.en: Yeah, visceral, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，直击内心，完全如此。

sentences.en: So the obvious questions are, you know, why would you do such a thing?
sentences.zh: 所以显而易见的问题是，你知道的，为什么要做出这种事？

sentences.en: Who could do it?
sentences.zh: 谁能干得出来？

sentences.en: And actually, who's the woman?
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个女人是谁？

sentences.en: Like, who is the victim?
sentences.zh: 比如，受害者是谁？

sentences.en: Because it's very hard for them to identify who the victims are.
sentences.zh: 因为他们很难确定受害者是谁。

sentences.en: So to start with the killer, they are completely bewildered right from the beginning.
sentences.zh: 先从凶手说起，他们从一开始就完全被迷糊了。

sentences.en: Like, why would anyone do this in such a savage and bestial way?
sentences.zh: 比如，怎么会有人以如此残忍和野蛮的方式做出这种事？

sentences.en: And also the fact that it's been done in streets down which people could be walking at any moment.
sentences.zh: 而且事实是，这居然发生在人们随时可能走过的街道上。

sentences.en: Well, we talked about the sense of the killer being a ghoul or a phantom or a specter.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们讨论过凶手具有食尸鬼、幻影或幽灵的感觉。

sentences.en: And there is, from the beginning, something strange about his ability to inflict these terrible murders in a public place,
sentences.zh: 而且从一开始，他在公共场所实施这些可怕谋杀的能力就有些诡异，

sentences.en: even though it is a kind of, you know, a street in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 尽管这算是一个半夜里的街道，你知道的。

sentences.en: So a policeman on his beat, he had walked down Buck's Row half an hour before Lechmere and Paul discovered the body.
sentences.zh: 所以一名巡警在莱克米尔和保尔发现尸体前半小时，曾走过巴克斯罗（Buck's Row）。

sentences.en: So that's, well, that's 10 past three in the morning.
sentences.zh: 所以那是，嗯，那是凌晨3点10分。

sentences.en: And he hadn't seen anything.
sentences.zh: 而他什么也没看见。

sentences.en: And no one had heard anything either.
sentences.zh: 而且也没有任何人听到任何声音。

sentences.en: And there was a woman called Mrs. Emma Green, who lived directly above the scene of the murder,
sentences.zh: 有一个叫埃玛·格林（Emma Green）太太的女人，住在谋杀现场的正上方，

sentences.en: who she said she was a light sleeper and had a scream been given, she would have heard it, you know, but not a peep.
sentences.zh: 她说她觉很轻，如果有人发出尖叫，她肯定会听到，你知道的，但一点声音也没有。

sentences.en: And there were watchmen too nearby.
sentences.zh: 附近也有守夜人。

sentences.en: They had heard nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们什么也没听到。

sentences.en: So it's evident to the inquest that the murderer must have slit his victim's throat before she'd been able to make a noise.
sentences.zh: 所以研讯很明显地表明，凶手一定是在受害者无法发出声音之前就割断了她的喉咙。

sentences.en: So either he'd strangled her or clasped her mouth or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以要么是他勒死了她，要么是捂住了她的嘴诸如此类的。

sentences.en: He'd done his terrible work with incredible speed.
sentences.zh: 他以惊人的速度完成了他可怕的罪行。

sentences.en: And then before Lechmere arrives, he must have kind of vanished into presumably the early morning traffic on Whitechapel Road and, you know, become part of the crowd.
sentences.zh: 然后，在莱克米尔到达之前，他一定已经消失在白教堂路清晨的车流中，你知道的，融入了人群。

sentences.en: And as you say, he must have been covered with blood.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他身上一定沾满了血。

sentences.en: There's an awful, must have been an awful lot of blood.
sentences.zh: 那场面太可怕了，一定有大量的血。

sentences.en: And yet, you know, he hasn't gone, no, no one has spotted him.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道的，他并没有离开，不，没有人发现他。

sentences.en: And that may be because he has a modus operandi that allows him to escape the worst of the blood spattering from the body.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为他有一种作案手法，让他能够避开尸体喷溅出的绝大部分血迹。

sentences.en: Or it may be because, as you said at the beginning, there are a lot of slaughterhouses and butcher shops and so on.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是因为，正如你一开始所说，有很多屠宰场、肉铺等等。

sentences.en: And a man walking down the street in an apron, you know, in the dark with bloodstains will actually go relatively unnoticed.
sentences.zh: 一个系着围裙、在黑暗中带着血迹走在街上的男人，实际上相对不会引人注目。

sentences.en: I mean, just on that topic, we're not the rest is true crime.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就这个话题而言，我们可不是什么真实犯罪播客。

sentences.en: And my knowledge of details of autopsies is not great.
sentences.zh: 我对尸检细节的了解并不多。

sentences.en: But I gather that if someone is strangled and then the throat is cut, there is much less blood.
sentences.zh: 但我了解到，如果一个人被勒死然后割喉，血会少得多。

sentences.en: I mean, of course, there is blood, but I gather this as a detail and perhaps people with more medical knowledge than us can confirm that for us.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当然会有血，但我收集到这个细节，也许医学知识比我们丰富的人可以为我们证实这一点。

sentences.en: Tom, I can't believe you're being so hesitant.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我真不敢相信你这么犹豫不决。

sentences.en: Anyway, tell us about the victim.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，跟我们讲讲受害者吧。

sentences.en: As you say, to begin with, the police are worried it's going to be difficult to identify her.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，一开始，警方担心很难确认她的身份。

sentences.en: She is examined by Dr. Llewellyn.
sentences.zh: 她接受了卢万医生的检查。

sentences.en: In his report, he says that she's a woman of small stature, that she's middle-aged.
sentences.zh: 他在报告中说，她身材矮小，是个中年妇女。

sentences.en: She has graying hair.
sentences.zh: 她有着灰白的头发。

sentences.en: She has a scar on her forehead.
sentences.zh: 她额头上有一个伤疤。

sentences.en: And he specifies one tooth deficient front of upper jaw.
sentences.zh: 他具体指出上颌前部缺一颗牙。

sentences.en: But that's nothing unusual.
sentences.zh: 但那没什么不寻常的。

sentences.en: Lots of people in, you know, in Whitechapel have lost a tooth or two.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，白教堂里的很多人都少了一两颗牙。

sentences.en: She has very few possessions on her, a comb, a looking glass, a handkerchief.
sentences.zh: 她身上带的物品非常少，一把梳子、一面镜子、一块手帕。

sentences.en: None of these give any hint as to her identity.
sentences.zh: 这些都没有提供任何关于她身份的线索。

sentences.en: And her clothing, too, is very anonymous.
sentences.zh: 而且她的衣服也非常大众化。

sentences.en: It's shabby.
sentences.zh: 很破旧。

sentences.en: It's stained.
sentences.zh: 有污渍。

sentences.en: The only exception is that she has a new bonnet.
sentences.zh: 唯一的例外是她有一顶新帽子。

sentences.en: Dr. Llewellyn specified it's made of black straw and it is trimmed with black velvet.
sentences.zh: 卢万医生具体说明那是黑草帽，并用黑天鹅绒装饰。

sentences.en: So is that enough to identify her?
sentences.zh: 那么这足以认出她吗？

sentences.en: Well, as it turns out, it is.
sentences.zh: 好吧，事实证明，确实够了。

sentences.en: Because within only a few hours of her body being found, the police have a name, Polly.
sentences.zh: 因为在发现她尸体短短几个小时内，警方就得到了一个名字：波莉（Polly）。

sentences.en: And their source is an elderly woman called Ellen Holland.
sentences.zh: 他们的消息来源是一个叫埃伦·霍兰德（Ellen Holland）的老妇人。

sentences.en: So maybe an ancestor.
sentences.zh: 所以也许是个祖先。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And Ellen had shared a room with Polly in a Doss house on Thrall Street, which is one of the notorious streets in the heart of Spitalfields.
sentences.zh: 埃伦曾与波莉在斯皮塔尔菲尔德（Spitalfields）核心臭名昭著的街道之一——特勒尔街（Thrall Street）的一家收容所共用一个房间。

sentences.en: So that's one clue.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个线索。

sentences.en: They still don't have a surname, but this will come very shortly.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然没有姓氏，但这很快就会揭晓。

sentences.en: Because when the police investigate Polly's petticoats, they find that they are stamped with the mark of a workhouse.
sentences.zh: 因为当警方调查波莉的衬裙时，他们发现上面盖有济贫院的印记。

sentences.en: And to be precise, the workhouse in Lambeth in South London.
sentences.zh: 确切地说，是伦敦南部兰贝斯（Lambeth）的济贫院。

sentences.en: And they find an inmate of that workhouse who is brought to inspect Polly's corpse.
sentences.zh: 他们找到了该济贫院的一名院友，被带来检查波莉的尸体。

sentences.en: And this person provides the police with Polly's real name, which is Mary Ann Nichols.
sentences.zh: 这个人向警方提供了波莉的真实姓名，也就是玛丽·安·尼科尔斯（Mary Ann Nichols）。

sentences.en: And the police go and they find that Mary Ann Nichols, Polly, has a father who's still alive and she has a husband.
sentences.zh: 警察去调查后发现，玛丽·安·尼科尔斯，也就是波莉，有一个仍然在世的父亲和一个丈夫。

sentences.en: And the following day on the 1st of September, Edward Walker, Polly's father, and William
sentences.zh: 第二天，即9月1日，波莉的父亲爱德华·沃克（Edward Walker）和威廉

sentences.en: Nichols, her husband, are brought to inspect her body.
sentences.zh: 她的丈夫尼科尔斯（Nichols）被带来检查她的尸体。

sentences.en: And William Nichols, the husband, he gazes down at the corpse of his dead wife, horribly mutilated as it is.
sentences.zh: 丈夫威廉·尼科尔斯凝视着他死去的妻子那满目疮痍、惨遭肢解的尸体。

sentences.en: And he breaks down and he has to be comforted by the police inspector.
sentences.zh: 他崩溃了，不得不由警督来安慰他。

sentences.en: And through his tears, he stammers, I forgive you as you are.
sentences.zh: 他泪流满面地结结巴巴地说，你现在这样，我原谅你。

sentences.en: I forgive you on account of what you have been to me.
sentences.zh: 看在你曾经对我的份上，我原谅你。

sentences.en: I mean, that's a very, it's a very Dickensian scene.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个非常，这是一个非常狄更斯式的场景。

sentences.en: And actually, the whole story that unfolds of Polly Nichols does have a kind of Dickensian
sentences.zh: 事实上，关于波莉·尼科尔斯的整个故事确实有一种狄更斯式的

sentences.en: arc to it, although a Dickensian arc in which, you know, they don't live happily ever after, but the heroine plunges into the abyss and never, ever recovers.
sentences.zh: 弧光，尽管这是一个狄更斯式的弧光，你知道的，他们并没有从此幸福地生活在一起，而是女主角陷入深渊，再也无法自拔。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think the kind of quality of a Dickens novel hangs over, as you say, completely hangs over her story.
sentences.zh: 我认为狄更斯小说的某种特质笼罩着，正如你所说，完全笼罩着她的故事。

sentences.en: So Polly Nichols, let's call her that.
sentences.zh: 所以波莉·尼科尔斯，我们就这么叫她吧。

sentences.en: She was born in 1845, just off Fleet Street, which today, you know, it's so grand that very few people can afford to live there.
sentences.zh: 她出生于1845年，就在弗利特街（Fleet Street）附近，如今，你知道的，那里如此宏伟，以至于极少数人能负担得起住在那里。

sentences.en: Very few people live there at all.
sentences.zh: 极少数人根本住在那里。

sentences.en: But back then, it was, again, a little bit like Spitalfields in 1888, a kind of warren of alleys and courtyards lined with dilapidated housing, so verging on a rookery.
sentences.zh: 但当年，它又有点像1888年的斯皮塔尔菲尔德，是一片错综复杂的小巷和庭院，里面排列着破旧的住房，几乎算得上是一个贫民窟。

sentences.en: But her parents, I mean, they're poor, but they're certainly not indigent.
sentences.zh: 但她的父母，我的意思是，他们很穷，但绝对不是赤贫。

sentences.en: So her father was a locksmith.
sentences.zh: 所以她的父亲是个锁匠。

sentences.en: Her mother was a laundress.
sentences.zh: 她的母亲是个洗衣妇。

sentences.en: And they belong to the ranks, I guess, of what Victorians would have called the respectable poor.
sentences.zh: 我想，他们属于维多利亚时代人所说的正派穷人的行列。

sentences.en: They have careers.
sentences.zh: 他们有工作。

sentences.en: As is very usual in this period, Polly loses a mother early on.
sentences.zh: 正如这一时期非常普遍的情况一样，波莉很早就失去了母亲。

sentences.en: So she dies of TB.
sentences.zh: 所以她死于肺结核。

sentences.en: But Edward Walker continues to provide for his family.
sentences.zh: 但爱德华·沃克继续养家糊口。

sentences.en: And this is very Dickens.
sentences.zh: 这非常狄更斯。

sentences.en: Polly steps into her mother's shoes, even though she's still just a young girl, and essentially takes over the maternal role.
sentences.zh: 波莉继承了母亲的衣钵，尽管她当时还只是个年轻女孩，却基本上承担起了母亲的角色。

sentences.en: So looking after her father in the way that little Mel looks after her grandfather or little
sentences.zh: 就像小尼尔（Nell）照顾她的祖父那样照顾她的父亲，或者小

sentences.en: Dorit looks after her father.
sentences.zh: 多丽特（Dorit）照顾她的父亲。

sentences.en: It's kind of very, you know, very reminiscent of that.
sentences.zh: 这有点非常，你知道的，非常让人联想到那个。

sentences.en: And the tone of a morally improving Dickensian melodrama seems to continue when, at the age of 18, Polly meets a printer's machiniSt.
sentences.zh: 而一部具有道德提升作用的狄更斯式情节剧的基调似乎还在继续，当时18岁的波莉遇到了一名印刷厂机械师。

sentences.en: Because Fleet Street, of course, is the center of the press.
sentences.zh: 因为弗利特街当然是媒体的中心。

sentences.en: And so that's exactly the kind of person that Polly might hope to meet, someone working for the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是波莉可能希望遇到的人，一个为报社工作的人。

sentences.en: And this is her husband, William Nichols, the guy who comes and sobs over her mutilated corpse in due course.
sentences.zh: 而这就是她的丈夫，威廉·尼科尔斯，也就是那个日后会在她惨遭虐杀的尸体旁痛哭流涕的家伙。

sentences.en: And they move out of Fleet Street.
sentences.zh: 他们搬出了弗利特街。

sentences.en: They move to Woolworth in South London.
sentences.zh: 他们搬到了伦敦南部伍尔维奇。

sentences.en: Polly's father goes with them.
sentences.zh: 波莉的父亲也跟着他们一起去了。

sentences.en: They start a family.
sentences.zh: 他们开始组建家庭。

sentences.en: Polly ends up having five children.
sentences.zh: 波莉最终生了五个孩子。

sentences.en: And it's a seeming model of domesticity.
sentences.zh: 这看起来像是一个家庭美满的模范。

sentences.en: A mother, a father, you know, a grandfather, children, very kind of like something out of
sentences.zh: 有母亲、父亲，你知道的，还有祖父、孩子们，非常像某种出自

sentences.en: Dickens.
sentences.zh: 狄更斯小说里的场景。

sentences.en: So then in 1880, Polly's by now 35.
sentences.zh: 接着到了1880年，此时波莉已经35岁了。

sentences.en: There is a spectacular bust up.
sentences.zh: 爆发了一场惊人的争吵。

sentences.en: And Polly walks out on her husband, out on her five children.
sentences.zh: 波莉抛弃了丈夫和五个孩子，一走了之。

sentences.en: One of them's just very, very young, barely an infant.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个孩子非常非常小，几乎还是个婴儿。

sentences.en: And she never returns.
sentences.zh: 她再也没有回来。

sentences.en: And that's her family broken up.
sentences.zh: 她的家庭就这样破裂了。

sentences.en: And there's different accusations, aren't there?
sentences.zh: 人们有各种各样的指责，对吧？

sentences.en: And actually, so family breakdown is a theme of almost all the victim stories, one way or another.
sentences.zh: 事实上，家庭破裂几乎是所有受害人故事的主题，以这样或那样的方式。

sentences.en: The collapse of a relationship.
sentences.zh: 一段关系的破裂。

sentences.en: But another theme is alcohol.
sentences.zh: 但另一个主题是酒精。

sentences.en: I mean, in almost all of the cases, alcohol is a huge factor.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在几乎所有的案例中，酒精都是一个巨大的因素。

sentences.en: And William later claimed that Polly had become an alcoholic, didn't he?
sentences.zh: 威廉后来声称波莉后来变成了酒鬼，不是吗？

sentences.en: And which may well have been true.
sentences.zh: 这很可能是真的。

sentences.en: Polly, it seems that she thought he'd begun an affair with a younger woman who'd been helping with the childcare.
sentences.zh: 看起来，波莉认为他和一个曾帮忙照顾孩子的年轻女子有了外遇。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是这样吧？

sentences.en: And both those things may have been true, that A, she was drinking, and B, he was having an affair.
sentences.zh: 这两件事可能都是真的，即第一，她在酗酒；第二，他有外遇。

sentences.en: And either way, what we will see again and again with the lives of these women is that something goes horribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，我们在这些女性的生平中会一次又一次地看到，事情会变得极其糟糕。

sentences.en: And you end up in a spiral.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会陷入一种恶性循环。

sentences.en: And in this world of late Victorian Britain, you know, no welfare state or not one worthy of
sentences.zh: 在维多利亚时代晚期的这个世界里，你知道的，没有福利国家，或者说没有什么名副其实的福利，

sentences.en: the name, once you're in the spiral, it is very, very hard to get out of it and to clamber back.
sentences.zh: 一旦你陷入这种循环，就非常非常难摆脱，也很难再爬上来。

sentences.en: And basically, you know, it's like a game of snakes and ladders and you're on a snake that is leading all the way to the bottom, i.e. to Whitechapel.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你知道的，这就像是一场蛇梯棋，你踩上了一条一直通往底部的蛇，也就是说，通往白教堂。

sentences.en: I mean, there is a kind of welfare and anyone who's read Oliver Twist will know what that welfare is because it comes in the form of the workhouse.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，确实有一种福利，任何读过《雾都孤儿》的人都会知道那是什么福利，因为它以贫民习艺所的形式出现。

sentences.en: And from this point on, if Polly's story is Dickensian, it's in that Oliver Twist sense.
sentences.zh: 从这一点开始，如果说波莉的故事带有狄更斯式的色彩，那也是《雾都孤儿》那种意义上的色彩。

sentences.en: She is plunging into a world of workhouses, of DOS houses, of a kind of desperate struggle on the streets to survive.
sentences.zh: 她正陷入一个充满习艺所、贫民收容所的世界，在街头进行着一种绝望的生存挣扎。

sentences.en: And she, understandably, to cope with the horrors of this, she turns to drink more and more.
sentences.zh: 可以理解的是，为了应对这些恐怖的事情，她越来越依赖酒精。

sentences.en: And her every attempt to kind of claw her way back up to try and find a solid footing again, kind of found us on the fact that she is becoming more and more of an alcoholic.
sentences.zh: 她每一次试图靠自己重新爬起来、重新找回稳固脚跟的尝试，都以失败告终，因为她越来越酗酒。

sentences.en: And by December 1887, you know, she is homeless and she joins the ranks of the homeless in
sentences.zh: 到1887年12月，你知道的，她已经无家可归了，并加入了特拉法加广场流浪者的行列，但她搬到特拉法加广场是在“血腥星期日”的一个月之后。

sentences.en: Trafalgar Square, but she's moved to Trafalgar Square a month after Bloody Sunday.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，当时警方已经清场了特拉法加广场，因此警方绝不可能允许无家可归者重新占据那个公共空间。

sentences.en: So, you know, when the police had cleared Trafalgar Square and so the police are in no mood to allow the homeless to reoccupy that public space.
sentences.zh: 因此，波莉是被警方驱赶到习艺所的一群女性之一，警察一路列队穿过街道去处理这件事。

sentences.en: And so Polly is one of a number of women who are moved on by the police to a workhouse and the police are kind of marching through the streets to be processed.
sentences.zh: 但波莉和其他10名女性设法溜走了，融入了小街道中，她们回到了特拉法加广场，在那里被正式逮捕。

sentences.en: But Polly and 10 other women managed to slip away and kind of melt into the side streets and they return to Trafalgar Square and there they are formally arrested.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，波莉已经醉了，逮捕她的警官形容她是广场上最不可理喻的女人。

sentences.en: And by this point, Polly is drunk and she's described by the arresting officer as having been the worst woman in the square.
sentences.zh: 这一次，她们没能甩掉警察的押送，波莉和其他10名女性最终都回到了习艺所。

sentences.en: And this time they are unable to slip their police escort and Polly and the other 10 women all end up back in the workhouse.
